turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Well, hi, it's nice to meet you too, doctor. I suppose what brings me in today... well, it's a bit of a story, honestly. See, I work as a personal care aide, and we have these regular staff meetings, you know, to go over protocols and patient updates and all that. And, well, the other day we were in one of these meetings, and the supervisor started talking about fall prevention. Now, fall prevention is huge in my line of work, just huge. You wouldn't believe the things that can happen if you aren't careful. So, I was listening, and I just... I got so incredibly worked up about it. The ideas were just racing through my head, so fast and so vivid, and before I even really knew what was happening, I was up out of my seat. I started acting out this entire, elaborate fall-prevention drill right there in the middle of the room. I was dragging chairs around to show obstacles, and my arms were just waving everywhere, demonstrating how to catch someone, how to brace them, the whole nine yards. And the thing is, I just couldn't seem to stop. People were staring, and a couple of folks even told me to sit down, to just take a breath, but I couldn't. I just kept going and going until I finally ran out of steam. My boss said I needed to come see someone, so... here I am.

symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient describes getting up out of their seat during a staff meeting and being unable to sit back down when asked.
symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient describes severely disturbed and inappropriate behavior, acting out an elaborate drill with chairs and waving arms during a meeting and being unable to stop.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been needing much less sleep than usual lately and still felt full of energy?
turns.patient_response:
You know, it's funny you ask about sleep, because... well, honestly, I just haven't really needed much of it at all lately. It’s like my body just decided it’s a waste of time. I’ll lay down, maybe around midnight or so, and then... boom. Two, maybe three hours later, my eyes just snap wide open. And it'll be way before dawn, I mean pitch black outside, the whole neighborhood is dead silent, but I wake up feeling absolutely fantastic. Just completely ready to go, like I just slept for a solid ten hours. 

And the thing is, I don't even think anything is wrong with it, you know? Like, it doesn't strike me as strange at all in the moment. I'll just get out of bed, go out to the kitchen, maybe make a pot of coffee, and I'll just be up making plans while the house is still dark. I'll sit there figuring out new daily routines for my patients, or how to reorganize the supply closets at work, just writing everything down and getting it all sorted out in my head. I just have so much energy, I really don't see the point in just lying there in bed staring at the ceiling when I could be getting a head start on the entire day. Even if the sun isn't even close to coming up yet, it just feels so good to be productive, so why would I just lay there? I just get right to it.

symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient explicitly states having 'so much energy' and feeling 'completely ready to go' despite very little sleep.
symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient reports only needing two or three hours of sleep and waking up feeling fully rested and ready for the day.
symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient describes an increase in goal-directed activity, specifically making plans for work, figuring out routines for patients, and reorganizing supply closets in the middle of the night.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been hearing voices that other people can’t hear?
turns.patient_response:
Well, you know, it’s strange you bring that up. Voices. It’s... I wouldn't call it voices, like people having a whole conversation in my head or anything crazy like that. But, well, yes, I suppose I have been hearing things. It happens mostly when it's quiet, which is rare enough, but like when I'm alone in the hallway at work, or maybe at home when I'm down by the laundry room. It’s always when there’s just this hum of the machines or the AC, you know? 

And out of nowhere, clear as day, I’ll hear my name. Just... 'Hey,' or someone calling out for me. Or, and this is the one that really gets my heart rate up, I'll hear one of the residents calling for help. And I mean, in my line of work, if you hear 'Help!' you drop everything. You don't think, you just move. So I’ll drop the laundry basket, or I’ll spin around in the hall, and I’ll go rushing over to check on them, checking the rooms, looking around the corner... and there's nobody there. Not a soul. It's just empty space. And I'll stand there for a minute, just listening, waiting to hear it again, but it's just quiet. It really throws you off, you know? Because I swear I heard it, loud and clear, but then... nothing. It makes you second-guess your own ears, honestly.

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly describes hearing their name or a resident calling for help 'clear as day' when no one is actually there.

turns.doctor_question: Have you heard those voices only when you’ve been feeling unusually energized like this?
turns.patient_response:
Well, no, not exactly. See, that’s the thing that really gets me, because you'd think it would all be tied together, right? Like, the engine revs up, and all the bells and whistles go off at the same time. But it hasn't always been like that. 

There was this stretch... oh, I don't know, a while back, where things actually felt pretty calm. I was actually sleeping, you know? Like a normal person. I’d go to bed, close my eyes, and wake up when the sun was actually shining, maybe get six or seven hours. And I wasn't doing all that rushing around, either. I didn't have the urge to reorganize the supply closets or map out everyone's daily schedule before dawn. I was just going to work, doing my shifts, coming home, and making dinner. Just regular, everyday stuff. 

But even then, even when I was feeling totally level and not all fired up with energy, I was still hearing it. For weeks, actually. I'd be walking down the hall, totally calm, and I'd still hear my name being called. 'Hey,' or just my name, clear as a bell. And I'd turn around, and still... nobody. And it wasn't just the hearing things, either. During that whole calm period, I was absolutely convinced—and I mean, I couldn't shake the feeling no matter how much I tried to reason with myself—that the people at work, the other aides, the nurses, even the supervisor, that they were keeping notes on me. I just knew they were watching everything I did, writing it down in some file somewhere, keeping track of every little mistake or every time I took a breath. It was just this heavy, nagging feeling that never went away, even when I was sleeping fine and not feeling all that extra energy. So, yeah, it definitely happens even when I'm not running on all cylinders.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient describes a fixed, false belief that coworkers and supervisors were secretly watching them and keeping notes on their every move.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient reports clearly hearing their name being called when no one is around.

I wasn't buzzing with all that crazy energy, I wasn't staying up all night making lists or reorganizing the closets, and I was actually getting a solid night's sleep. I felt totally level, you know? Just going to work, doing my job, coming home, watching a little TV, and going to bed. 

But even during those weeks, when everything else felt so calm and regular, I was still dealing with it. I'd still be walking down the hall at work and hear my name called out, clear as day, and turn around to find an empty hallway. And that whole time, I was still completely, one hundred percent convinced that my coworkers were keeping some kind of secret file on me, writing down notes about everything I did. It just didn't stop, even when my mood was totally normal. It was like those things just kept going on their own schedule, no matter how rested or calm I was feeling. So yeah, it definitely lasted for weeks like that without the energy or the mood stuff.
